The app is built, verified, and running. Here's the handover.

## Your bookmark app is ready — **http://maker:4000**

It opens on the clean first-run screen; save your first link and everything else comes to life.

**Everything we agreed on is implemented:**
- **Save in one step** — paste a link; its real title, description, and icon fill in automatically (I confirmed live fetching works).
- **Tag** one at a time with reuse suggestions; remove with the ×.
- **Notes** — add, edit, or clear your own reminder on any link.
- **Reading list** — opt-in with *＋ Reading list*; *Done* clears it from the queue but keeps the link saved.
- **Find** — search across title, description, address, tags, and notes, with tag-click filtering, and the two combine; matches are highlighted.
- **Remove** with a confirm step.
- **Rough edges:** a page whose details can't be read is still saved (you add a title/description by hand); duplicates take you to the existing one instead of copying; non-links are gently blocked; empty screens give a calm prompt.

## Verification report (all passed)

I tested against every approved behaviour:
- **10 browser acceptance tests** — one per scenario (SCN-001 through SCN-009), driving the real app end-to-end in Chromium.
- **23 unit/API tests** — the search/tag/duplicate/URL rules, page-info parsing, the server endpoints, and data durability across a restart.

**Total: 33/33 passing.** Your data is stored on the server so it persists across restarts.

Recorded for a **later cycle** (not built now, as we agreed): large-collection performance/paging, cross-device sync, export/backup, and a couple of smaller refinements.

**Do you accept this software as meeting the behaviours we approved, and agree to complete this cycle?** Once you confirm, I'll close out the cycle and log the result.
